assessments.reasoning: GNU’s fdl-1.3.txt identifies the 3 November 2008 edition. Its own bytes [3327,3605) define Cover Texts and [7115,8127) state the trigger and both placement paragraphs. The following Opaque-copy paragraph uses a different trigger and does not broaden the covered media for this claim.

challenge.method: Test 100 printed copies with listed texts, then 101 copies in each qualifying medium and in a download-only medium without customary printed covers. At 101 qualifying copies, test an empty Cover Text list and a list too long for the back cover.
challenge.results: The 100-copy case and the download-only case described fail this trigger. Both qualifying media pass at 101 if texts are required. A notice requiring none leaves the cover-text duty untriggered. With back-cover overflow, §3 advises keeping as many of the earliest listed back texts there as reasonably fit and continuing the rest on adjacent pages. The specific arrangement is advisory even though carrying the required texts is mandatory.

limitations: The Addendum illustrates a work notice. Its example cannot establish the Cover Texts of a particular Document.
Publisher identification, title presentation and the separate Opaque-copy provision lie outside this placement claim.
reasoning: GNU FDL 1.3 §3 requires clear, legible placement of required front and back texts on the corresponding covers. Three conditions operate together. The publisher issues more than 100 copies, those copies are printed or in a medium commonly having printed covers, and the Document’s notice requires Cover Texts.
